text:
jamal: Heads-up — we've seen ~18 small bursts in eu-west1/gpu this week where 1-3 short-lived jobs appear, CA spins up a node, then 30-90s later the node is gone and we get churn + networking flaps. Cost and pod evictions spike. Anyone else seeing this?

maria: yeah saw the alerts. pattern looks like many pods with very short lifetimes + binpacking causing a whole node to be used for a single tiny job. CA thinks node is needed then immediately not needed.

kevin: screenshots? logs?

jamal: paste of events: ```
Warning FailedScheduling default/my-job-abc 0/8 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
Normal Scheduled default/my-job-abc to gpu-nodepool-eu-3
Normal Killing default/my-job-abc Container failed liveness probe
```

maria: two levers that helped us before: raise --scale-down-unneeded-time and add a short "warm" nodepool with small reserved capacity (1-2 nodes) so CA sees capacity and avoids one-off provisions.

kevin: Agreed. Also tweak scan interval and delay after add: 
- --scan-interval=20s -> keep short so we react fast to real demand
- --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m -> don't evict immediately on tiny dips
- --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m -> give new nodes a grace window

maria: And balance-similar-node-groups + prefer-better-packing helps reduce single-job node waste. We've been testing a priority label approach (nodepool priority) so expander prefers keeping higher-priority pools warm.

jamal: Can we try config: 
```
--expander=binpack
--scan-interval=20s
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m
--max-node-provision-time=8m
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
```
Also thinking of marking 1 node in gpu-eu pool as protected with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true` to act as a tiny buffer. Thoughts on ops risk?

kevin: protecting a node is ok short-term but be careful with long-term cost drift. Lambdas: better is a 1-node reserved pool with cheaper preemptible GPUs and `--ok-to-evict` behavior. That way we accept occasional evictions but avoid churn on expensive nodes.

maria: Network flap note: when CA cycles nodes fast we see CNI reattach delays and ephemeral route additions fail in cloud provider for a few seconds; that causes connection resets for pods doing heavy gRPC. So the cooldown also helps reliability, not just cost.

ops-jenkins: deploy bot: rolling update of cluster-autoscaler configmap to test these flags scheduled at 23:00 UTC. DRY-RUN logs attached.

infra-bot: incident/alert: gpu-eu churn spike suppressed after applying scale-down-unneeded-time=10m in canary (eu-test). Monitoring will check 6h window for churn metric < baseline.

jamal: Great — I'll leave the canary running. If the 6h lookgood, we can roll to prod and create a short RFC for a warm preemptible buffer + cost ops playbook. Thanks! :thumbsup:

kevin: Also we should document the threshold decision — what burst size/ttl justifies warm pool versus dynamic spin-up. I can sketch numbers tomorrow.

maria: FYI, remember to not set --scale-down-unneeded-time too high for dev clusters; they have low steady-state and we want cheap. We'll limit changes to gpu* pools only.

jamal: noted. will only target gpu-eu* and gpu-us* autoscaler configs. will post results later.
